ex_en: Bring a loaf of bread from the bakery with you.
note: Libyans usually say خبزة for bread in general; pl. خبز khubz. Often bought fresh twice a day.

phrases.en: The bread is hot right now
I'll buy bread and come back

en: tannūr bread (flatbread baked in a clay oven)
ex_ar: خبزة التنور مع الزيت حاجة باهية.
ex_en: Tannūr bread with olive oil is a lovely thing.
note: Traditional round flatbread baked on the walls of a clay tannūr, common in homes and rural areas.

phrases.en: I want tannūr bread with olive oil

phrases.ar: أمي تطيب خبزة التنور في الحوش
phrases.en: My mom bakes tannūr bread in the courtyard

ex_en: Today we're cooking rice with fish.
note: Also pronounced rozz. Libyan 'rice with fish' (رز بالحوت) is a classic coastal dish.

phrases.en: Is the rice cooked or not?

ex_en: Meat has become expensive these days.
note: Libyan pronunciation inserts a vowel: la7am. Without qualification it usually means lamb/mutton.

phrases.en: How much is a kilo of meat?

ex_en: I want a kilo of minced meat for the mbaṭṭan.

phrases.en: Give me half a kilo of minced meat
The minced meat is for the meatballs

ex_ar: لحم العلوش أحسن من لحم البقري.
ex_tr: la7am il-3allūsh a7san min la7am il-bagri.
ex_en: Lamb is better than beef.
note: علوش 3allūsh = young sheep/lamb in Libyan; lamb is the prestige meat.

ex_en: Beef is a bit cheaper.

ex_ar: في الجنوب ياكلوا لحم الجمل هلبة.
ex_tr: fi j-janūb yāklu la7am ij-jmal hallba.
ex_en: In the south they eat camel meat a lot.
note: Camel meat is sold at specialised butchers and is popular in winter.

phrases.en: Have you ever eaten camel meat?
Camel meat is a bit heavy

ex_en: I love liver grilled over charcoal.
note: Grilled liver is a traditional treat on Eid al-Adha.

ex_ar: أمي تدير القديد بعد العيد الكبير.
ex_tr: ummi tdīr il-gadīd ba3d il-3īd il-kbīr.
ex_en: My mother makes dried meat after Eid al-Adha.
note: Strips of sacrificial lamb salted, spiced and sun-dried; later cooked in sharba or with couscous.

phrases.en: The dried meat is hanging in the courtyard
Couscous with dried meat is tasty

ex_en: Dinner tonight is chicken in the oven.
note: Single bird: دجاجة djāja.

phrases.en: The chicken is done in the oven

ex_en: The fish is fresh in the market today.
note: In Libya حوت means any fish (not 'whale' as in MSA). pl. حيتان 7ītān.

phrases.en: How much is a kilo of fish?

ex_en: Put tuna in the sandwich.
note: Tuna is a staple filling with harīsa and olives.

ex_en: Fried sardines are cheap and tasty.
note: From Italian sardina.

phrases.en: We fry the sardines in the pan

ex_en: I want two fried eggs for breakfast.
note: Very Libyan word; collective/pl. دحي da7i. MSA بيض is understood but not used.

phrases.en: The eggs are finished in the fridge

ex_en: Our breakfast is bread, cheese and olives.
Put a little butter on the bread.

phrases.en: The butter is in the fridge
I'll fry the eggs in butter

ex_en: 3aSīda is eaten with ghee and honey.

phrases.en: Put a spoonful of ghee in the couscous
Traditional ghee has a strong smell

ex_en: Mountain honey is pricey but worth it.

phrases.en: Tea with honey for the cough

ex_en: I went to the market to buy vegetables.
note: Collective noun used for all vegetables.

phrases.en: Wash the vegetables before you cut them

ex_en: After lunch we eat some fruit.

phrases.en: I want to buy some fruit

ex_en: Tomatoes are the basis of every Libyan dish.
note: Single: حبة طماطم 7abbat TmāTim.

phrases.en: How much is a kilo of tomatoes?

ex_en: Chop the onion thinly.
note: Single: بصلة bSala.

ex_en: The soup needs a little garlic.
note: A clove: سنة ثوم sinnit thūm.

phrases.en: The smell of garlic is strong

ex_en: I want fried potatoes with the chicken.
note: Libyans say بطاطا, not Egyptian بطاطس.

ex_en: Put the carrots and potatoes in the stew.
note: Maghrebi word for carrots; جزر jazar is also understood.

ex_en: Hot pepper burns.
note: فلفل أخضر green pepper; فلفل حار hot pepper; فلفل أكحل black pepper.

ex_en: Add a little black pepper.
note: أكحل ak7al is the Libyan word for black.

phrases.en: The black pepper has run out

ex_en: The salad has cucumber and tomato.

phrases.en: The cucumber is fresh and cool

ex_en: Stuffed eggplant is very tasty.
We're making stuffed zucchini today.
note: Libyan قرعة / قرع gar3 = zucchini, not Egyptian كوسة. Same word also means 'bottle'.

phrases.en: Put the zucchini in the stew

ex_en: Stew with beans is a summer dish.

phrases.en: Sort the beans before you cook them

ex_ar: الفول المدمس فطور باهي في الشتا.
ex_en: Stewed fava beans are a good winter breakfast.

phrases.en: A fava bean sandwich with harissa

ex_en: Libyan soup has chickpeas in it.

phrases.en: A plate of chickpeas with cumin

ex_en: Lentil soup is warming in the cold.
Put the salad on the table.
note: From Italian insalata.

phrases.en: I want a salad without onion

ex_en: Chop some parsley over the salad.
note: Maghrebi form; Levantine بقدونس is not used.

phrases.en: A bunch of parsley for a dinar

ex_en: Fresh coriander gives a nice aroma.

phrases.en: Add a bit of dried coriander

ex_en: Mint tea, please.
note: Fresh mint is often added to green tea.

phrases.en: Put the mint in the teapot

ex_en: Apples are expensive this year.
note: Single: تفاحة tiffā7a.

ex_en: Orange juice is fresh and healthy.
note: Libyan has n at the end: برتقان, not برتقال. Single: برتقانة.

phrases.en: The oranges are sweet this year

ex_en: Kids love bananas.
note: Single: موزة mūza.

phrases.en: How much is a kilo of bananas?

ex_en: The grapes of Gharyan are famous.
In Ramadan we break the fast with dates and milk.
note: Libya grows many date varieties.

phrases.en: Eat a date with the milk
Dates from the south are better

ex_en: Pomegranates come in autumn.

phrases.en: Seed the pomegranate into a bowl

ex_en: Watermelon in summer cools you down.
note: Maghrebi word; Libyans do not use بطيخ for watermelon.

phrases.en: Cut the watermelon for the guests

ex_en: Fresh figs can't be passed up.
note: Maghrebi word for figs; MSA تين is rarely heard.

phrases.en: The fig tree in the courtyard

ex_en: The peaches are sweet this year.

phrases.en: The peaches are fresh at the market

ex_en: Apricot jam at breakfast.

phrases.en: I want half a kilo of apricots

ex_en: Black olives with the cheese.
Squeeze a bit of lemon on the fish.
Strawberry milkshake.
note: From Italian fragola.

ex_en: On Fridays we eat couscous.
note: Libyan couscous is usually served with lamb, chickpeas, potatoes and a spicy tomato sauce, often topped with an onion-raisin sauce (بصلة).

phrases.en: My mom is going to cook couscous today

en: bazin (barley dough dome served with sauce)
ex_ar: البازين ياكلوه باليد في قصعة وحدة.
ex_tr: il-bāzīn yāklūh bil-yadd fi gaS3a wa7da.
ex_en: Bazin is eaten by hand from one shared bowl.
note: National dish: a dome of barley flour dough surrounded by lamb, eggs and potato in a spicy tomato sauce.

phrases.en: Come eat bazin at our place

ex_en: I don't have time, I'll make mbakbka.
note: Pasta cooked directly in a spicy tomato-meat sauce; name imitates the 'bak-bak' bubbling sound.

ex_ar: في رمضان الشربة ما تغيبش على السفرة.
ex_tr: fi ramaDān ish-sharba ma tghībsh 3ala is-sufra.
ex_en: In Ramadan sharba never misses from the table.
note: شربة ليبية: tomato-lamb soup with orzo (lsān 3aSfūr), chickpeas and mint; essential at iftar.

phrases.en: Give me a bowl of soup

ex_ar: في المولد يديروا العصيدة بالرب والسمن.
ex_en: For the Prophet's birthday they make 3aSīda with date syrup and ghee.
note: Also served to celebrate a new baby. رب rubb = date syrup.

phrases.en: Asida in the morning for a new mother

ex_en: 3uSbān is an Eid al-Adha dish.
note: Tripe/intestine stuffed with rice, meat, herbs and spices; cooked in sauce or with couscous.

ex_en: The kids want pasta every day.
note: Italian legacy (maccheroni); pasta is daily food in Libya.

phrases.en: The pasta is done, drain it

en: baked pasta with meat and egg
ex_en: I made baked pasta for the guests.

phrases.en: The baked pasta is in the oven
I love baked pasta with cheese

ex_en: Rishta with chicken is a light dish.
note: Steamed noodles served with tomato sauce or chickpeas.

phrases.en: My grandma rolls the rishta by hand

en: mbaṭṭan (fried potato slices stuffed with meat)
ex_en: Mbaṭṭan is made in Ramadan.
note: Potato slices sandwiched with spiced minced meat, dipped in egg and fried.

phrases.en: I want two pieces of mbaṭṭan

ex_en: Meat būrīk goes with sharba.
note: Ottoman-origin börek; fried or baked pastry with meat, cheese or potato.

ex_en: Stuffed vegetables take a long time.

phrases.ar: المحشي متاع أمي ما فيه كيفه
phrases.tr: il-ma7shi mtā3 ummi ma fīh kīfah
phrases.en: Nothing beats my mom's stuffed vegetables

ex_en: 7rāymi is a Tripoli dish.
note: Spicy fish stew; also cooked with lamb in some homes.

ex_en: Shakshuka with dried meat is a heavy breakfast.
Bsīsa with oil and sugar fills you up.
note: Roasted grains and spices ground to a flour; mixed with olive oil. Traditional travel food.

phrases.en: Put the bsīsa in the milk

en: zummīta (roasted barley flour with oil and spices)
ex_en: My grandmother likes zummīta in the morning.
note: Similar to bsīsa; rural traditional food.

ex_en: Add more sauce to the couscous.

phrases.en: Give me a bit more sauce

ex_en: Put a spoonful of tomato paste in the pot.
note: From Italian salsa; in Libya it specifically means canned tomato paste.

phrases.en: The tomato paste ran out, bring a can
The sauce needs more tomato paste

ex_ar: الليبيين يحطوا الهريسة في كل شي.
ex_tr: il-lībiyyīn y7uTTu il-harīsa fi kull shay.
ex_en: Libyans put harissa in everything.
note: Not the Levantine semolina dessert.

phrases.en: Put a bit of harissa in the sandwich

ex_en: Libyan spice mix has cumin and turmeric.
note: The house blend is often called حرارات 7rārāt.

phrases.en: Add a bit of spice mix
The spices are from the spice seller

ex_en: Cumin goes with fish.

phrases.en: We're out of cumin at home

ex_en: Turmeric gives rice a yellow color.

phrases.en: A little turmeric in the soup

ex_en: There's cinnamon on top of the 3aSīda.

phrases.en: Put a cinnamon stick in the rice

ex_en: Our olive oil is from the mountain.
note: Plain زيت usually means olive oil; vegetable oil is زيت نباتي or زيت قلي.

phrases.en: The oil is hot, put in the potatoes

ex_en: Your tea has a lot of sugar.

phrases.en: The sugar's run out, bring a kilo

ex_en: The food needs a little salt.

phrases.en: The food is salty, I added too much salt

ex_en: Flour, oil and sugar from the cooperative.
note: ق → g. Barley flour for bāzīn is دقيق شعير.

phrases.en: A sack of flour for the bread
Flour got more expensive this month

ex_en: Couscous is made from semolina.
Bazin is made from barley flour.
The food is ready, come!
note: Very common Libyan/Maghrebi word for food.

ex_en: What do we have for breakfast?
note: In Ramadan فطور means the evening fast-breaking meal.

ex_en: Lunch is at three o'clock.
note: Lunch is the main meal of the day in Libya.

ex_en: Dinner is light tonight.
At suhoor we eat rice pudding.

phrases.en: I didn't have suhoor last night

ex_en: We brought sweets for the wedding.
note: Also used as adjective 'sweet'. Pastries for occasions are called حلويات 7alawiyyāt.

phrases.en: What do you have for dessert?

ex_en: Tripolitan makrūḍ is famous at Eid.
note: Diamond-shaped semolina pastry stuffed with date paste, fried and soaked in syrup or honey.

phrases.en: My mom will make makrūḍ for Eid

ex_en: Ghrība melts in the mouth.
note: Made of flour/semolina, ghee and sugar; an Eid staple.

ex_en: Almond baklava is expensive.

phrases.en: A kilo of baklava for Eid

ex_en: Savory ka3k with tea.
note: Libyan ka3k comes sweet or salted (with fennel/nigella).

ex_en: Sfinz with egg in the morning.
note: Fried ring of dough, eaten plain, with sugar/honey, or with an egg fried inside.

phrases.en: I want two sfinz with egg

ex_en: Zlābya is the Ramadan sweet.

ex_ar: العصيدة ما تحلاش من غير رب.
ex_tr: il-3aSīda ma ti7lāsh min ghēr rubb.
ex_en: 3aSīda isn't good without date syrup.

phrases.en: Put a bit of date syrup on the asida

ex_en: Bread with butter and jam.

phrases.en: My mom makes jam at home

ex_en: The little one wants chocolate.
note: From Italian cioccolata.

ex_en: Put the biscuits with the tea.

phrases.en: A pack of biscuits for the kids

ex_en: We made a cake for the birthday.

phrases.en: Cut me a piece of cake

ex_en: Let's go eat ice cream by the sea.
note: From Italian gelato; very Libyan.

ex_en: Tea with peanuts after lunch.
note: Roasted peanuts dropped into the third glass of tea are a Libyan signature.

ex_en: Tea with almonds for guests.
note: Toasted almonds in tea are a more festive alternative to peanuts.

ex_en: I want a tuna sandwich with harissa.
note: Street sandwiches are usually in a baguette-style loaf.

ex_en: Shall we have shawarma for dinner tonight?
Pizza is everyday food in Libya.
note: Italian legacy; often pronounced with p.

ex_en: Pasta with meatballs.
Wheat and barley from the mountain.

phrases.en: The wheat harvest is in summer

ex_en: In Zuwara the seafood is fresh.

phrases.en: A seafood restaurant by the sea

ex_en: Shrimp is very expensive.
note: From Italian gambero.

phrases.en: How much is a kilo of shrimp?

ex_en: Grilled fish with spicy salad.

phrases.en: I want grilled fish with rice
Grilled fish is healthier than fried

ex_en: The soup needs orzo.
note: Lit. 'bird's tongue'; essential in sharba lībiyya.

phrases.en: Put the orzo in the soup

ex_en: Rice pudding with cinnamon.
Give me a glass of water.
note: Libyan form of ماء.

phrases.en: The water is cut off today

ex_ar: نشروا مية معدنية، مية الحنفية مش باهية.
ex_tr: nishru mayya ma3daniyya, mayyat il-7anafiyya mush bāhya.
ex_en: We buy bottled water; the tap water isn't good.
note: Bottled water is the norm for drinking.

phrases.en: A big bottle of mineral water

ex_en: Come let's drink tea.
note: Libyans say شاهي. Tea is brewed strong, poured from height to make foam, and served in small glasses in three rounds.

ex_en: Red tea with foam.
note: Lit. 'red tea'; boiled long, very strong and sweet. Libyans call black tea 'red'.

phrases.en: I want a glass of black tea

ex_en: Green tea with mint.

phrases.en: Do you want black or green (tea)?

ex_en: The third round is tea with peanuts.
note: Usually the third, lightest round of tea.

phrases.en: Shall I make tea with peanuts?
Tea with peanuts is for guests

ex_en: Tea without foam isn't worth drinking.
note: Created by pouring tea back and forth between pot and glass from a height; a mark of a skilled tea-maker.

phrases.en: Make the foam bigger a bit

ex_en: I only drank the first round.
note: Libyan tea comes in three rounds (first strong/bitter, second sweeter, third with peanuts). Also means a metal cup/bowl.

phrases.en: Give me a glass of tea

ex_en: I want coffee without sugar.
note: ق → g. Also means a café (coffee shop).

phrases.en: Shall we go to the café?

ex_ar: جدي يشرب القهوة العربية من الززوة.
ex_tr: jiddi yishrab il-gahwa il-3arabiyya min iz-zazwa.
ex_en: My grandfather drinks Arabic coffee from the cezve.
note: Boiled ground coffee, served in small cups.

phrases.en: Shall I make you Arabic coffee?

ex_en: A macchiato, please.
note: From Italian macchiato; the signature Libyan café drink, often with lots of foam.

ex_en: The cappuccino here is good.
I want a double espresso.
Do you have instant coffee?
note: Brand name used generically.

phrases.en: I make instant coffee in the morning

ex_en: The milk has run out, bring a liter.
Cold buttermilk with couscous.
note: In Libya لبن is the sour drink left after churning butter, not plain milk.

ex_en: Rāyib is drunk in summer.

phrases.en: Curdled milk cools you in summer
Bring curdled milk from the shop

ex_en: Strawberry yogurt for the kids.

phrases.en: Put the yogurt in the fridge

ex_en: Banana-milk juice.
note: Thick fruit-milk blends are popular at juice shops.

phrases.en: What do you want, juice or soda?

ex_en: Bring a cold soda.
note: From Italian gassosa.

ex_en: Fresh lāgbi in the oases.
note: Sweet sap tapped from date palms; drunk fresh in the south and oases before it ferments.

phrases.en: Lāgbi is sweet when it's fresh

ex_en: Hot cocoa in the cold.

phrases.en: Cocoa with milk for the kids

ex_en: What drink do you want?

phrases.en: A cold drink or a hot one?

ex_en: Put ice in the juice.
A little orange-blossom water in the coffee.
note: Added to coffee and sweets for aroma.

phrases.en: A bottle of orange-blossom water from the spice seller

ex_en: Drink a herbal tea for your stomach.

phrases.en: I'll make a hot herbal tea

ex_en: Tea with extra sugar.
note: Libyan tea is typically very sweet.

ex_en: Coffee without sugar, please.
My mother is in the kitchen cooking.
note: From Italian cucina; also heard كوزينة kūzīna. MSA مطبخ is understood.

phrases.en: The kitchen is a bit small
What are you doing in the kitchen?

ex_en: Put the rice in a big plate.
note: pl. صحون S7ūn.

ex_en: A small cup of coffee.
note: pl. فناجين fnājīn.

ex_en: I drink milk from a mug.
Give me a spoon for the soup.
note: pl. معالق m3ālig. Note Libyan metathesis vs MSA ملعقة.

phrases.en: The spoons are in the drawer

ex_en: Pasta is eaten with a fork.
note: Older speakers may say فرشيطة from Italian forchetta.

phrases.en: I eat with a fork and knife

ex_en: This knife doesn't cut.
note: Feminine in Libyan. pl. سكاكين skākīn.

ex_en: The soup is in the pot on the fire.
note: pl. برم buram.

phrases.en: The pot has been on the fire since morning

ex_en: Fry the eggs in the pan.
note: From Turkish tava.

phrases.en: The pan is hot, be careful
Wash the pan after you fry

ex_en: Couscous is steamed in the kaskās.
note: Perforated pot set on top of the pot of sauce.

phrases.en: Put the steamer on top of the pot
My grandma's couscous steamer is old

ex_en: Put the chicken in the oven for an hour.
note: Libyan for both a home oven and the neighbourhood bakery.

phrases.en: I'm going to the bakery to get bread

ex_en: The gas oven is off.

phrases.en: Preheat the oven to two hundred

ex_en: The meat is in the freezer.

phrases.en: Take the meat out of the freezer

ex_en: Turn off the gas before you leave.
note: Also the cooking gas cylinder.

phrases.en: The gas ran out, change the cylinder
Light the gas under the pot

ex_en: The teapot is on the charcoal.
note: Small enamel/metal pot for Libyan tea, traditionally on a charcoal brazier (كانون kānūn).

ex_en: Tea on the brazier tastes better.

phrases.en: We warm ourselves at the brazier

ex_en: Bring the tea tray.
note: pl. صواني Swāni.

phrases.en: Carry the tray to the guests

ex_en: The bazin is in a big bowl.
note: Traditional wooden or metal bowl from which the family eats together.

phrases.en: We all eat from one bowl

ex_en: Give me the ladle so I can serve the soup.

phrases.en: The ladle is in the pot
Give me another ladle of soup

ex_en: Drain the pasta in the colander.

phrases.en: Wash the vegetables in the colander

ex_en: Crush the garlic in the mortar.

phrases.en: Pound the cumin in the mortar

ex_en: Make the coffee in the cezve.
note: From Turkish cezve.

phrases.en: The coffee pot is on the fire
The coffee pot is small, it's only enough for two

ex_en: Put the water in the kettle.
The juice is in the blender.

phrases.en: The blender makes a lot of noise
Put the banana and milk in the blender

ex_en: Heat the food in the microwave.
Bring a bottle of water from the fridge.
note: Same word as zucchini; context decides. pl. قراعي grā3i.

ex_en: The jam is in the jar.
Put the lid on the pot.

phrases.en: Where's the lid of the pot?

ex_en: A can of tomatoes and a can of tuna.
note: pl. علب 3ulab.

phrases.en: Open the can with the knife

ex_en: Who's going to wash the dishes?
note: Libyan collective for dishes/kitchenware.

ex_en: The sponge is old, replace it.

phrases.en: The sponge and soap are at the sink

ex_en: The dishes are in the sink.

phrases.en: Put the plates in the sink

en: dining spread; table set for a meal
ex_en: The table is ready, please come.
note: Often a cloth spread on the floor for a family meal.

ex_en: Do you have matches so I can light the gas?
note: Libyan word; MSA كبريت is understood.

ex_en: The tea is in the thermos for the trip.
Give me a napkin.
note: Paper tissues are often called كلينكس by brand name.

phrases.en: Wipe your hands with the napkin

ex_en: Chop the onion on the board.

phrases.en: Wash the board after the meat

ex_en: I don't have money now.
note: Plural in form; agreement often plural (الفلوس خلصوا).

ex_en: The price is ten dinars.
note: pl. دنانير dnānīr; after numbers 3–10 Libyans often keep the singular.

ex_en: Bread used to cost fifty dirhams.
note: 1 dinar = 1000 dirhams. pl. دراهم drāhim, also used loosely for 'money'.

phrases.en: I don't have a single dirham

ex_en: He doesn't have a single penny.
note: Old unit kept in idioms.

ex_en: Do you have change for ten dinars?
Take your change.

phrases.en: The change is one dinar short

ex_en: Keep the change.
What's the price of this?
note: Maghrebi word; سعر si3r is also used, esp. in news.

phrases.en: Lower the price a bit for me

ex_en: The dollar rate went up today.
note: pl. أسعار as3ār.

ex_en: How much is a kilo?
note: The basic shopping question.

phrases.en: How much is half a kilo?

ex_en: Entry is free.
note: Also means 'for nothing/in vain'. ببلاش bblāsh = for free.

ex_ar: الحانوت اللي في الزنقة يبيع كل شي.
ex_tr: il-7ānūt illi fiz-zanga ybī3 kull shay.
ex_en: The shop in the street sells everything.
note: pl. حوانيت 7wānīt.

phrases.en: I'm going to the shop, do you need anything?

ex_en: We go to the market on Friday.
note: ق → g. pl. أسواق aswāg. Weekly markets are named for the day (سوق الجمعة, سوق الثلاثاء).

phrases.en: I bought it at the market

ex_en: The new supermarket has everything.

phrases.en: The supermarket is open till ten

ex_en: The shop is closed on Friday.
note: pl. محلات ma7allāt.

phrases.en: He opened a new shop on the street

ex_en: Let's go to the mall in the evening.
The vegetable market opens early.

phrases.en: I bought the tomatoes at the vegetable market

ex_en: Fresh fish is at the fish market.

phrases.en: I'll go to the fish market early

ex_en: The butcher cut the meat for me.

phrases.en: Tell the butcher to mince the meat

ex_en: The baker starts work at dawn.
note: The bakery itself is الكوشة.

phrases.en: My brother works as a baker

ex_en: This greengrocer sells at a good price.
